# CodingAgent.in

Sovereign, open-source, local-LLM-first agentic engineering platform for AI coding agents, MCP-native tooling, and verification-first workflows. Architecture and direction only — live execution requires a configured backend.

Public knowledge surface (canonical URLs):
- https://codingagent.in/
- https://codingagent.in/pillars
- https://codingagent.in/platform
- https://codingagent.in/agent-modes
- https://codingagent.in/local-runtimes
- https://codingagent.in/security-matrix
- https://codingagent.in/faq

# Pillar details

## CodingAgent AI Coding Agents (https://codingagent.in/ai-coding-agents)
Category: Core & Agents
Autonomous systems combining generative model reasoning, repository-scale context, tool execution, and deterministic verification gates.
Rationale: Moves beyond interactive chat windows into controlled engineering systems with explicit state tracking and execution boundaries.
Verification aspect: Requires acceptance gates that validate code behavior rather than model verbal claims.

## CodingAgent Agentic Engineering (https://codingagent.in/agentic-engineering)
Category: Core & Agents
Disciplined methodology for designing, governing, testing, and deploying semi-autonomous software engineering agents.
Rationale: Applies rigorous systems engineering practices to AI agent architectures, replacing ad-hoc prompts with structured contracts.
Verification aspect: Pre-flight policy audits, continuous unit test gates, and deterministic build artifacts.

## CodingAgent Plan-Execute-Verify (https://codingagent.in/plan-execute-verify)
Category: Core & Agents
The core tri-phasic execution loop ensuring planning is isolated from execution, and execution is gated by independent verification.
Rationale: Prevents runaway tool calling and hallucinations by enforcing plan approval before execution and test evidence before completion.
Verification aspect: Independent test runner, compiler type-checker, and linter pass as strict criteria.

## CodingAgent Task Graphs (https://codingagent.in/task-graphs)
Category: Core & Agents
Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) representing complex engineering goals broken down into interdependent, atomically executable work units.
Rationale: Enables parallelization of independent refactors, safe rollbacks of failed nodes, and transparent progress visualization.
Verification aspect: Node-level acceptance criteria verified before downstream dependent nodes receive execution locks.

## CodingAgent Agent State Machines (https://codingagent.in/agent-state-machines)
Category: Core & Agents
Deterministic finite state machines governing agent lifecycle transitions, error recovery, and tool access authorizations.
Rationale: Eliminates unpredictable cyclic loops where models endlessly retry failing shell commands without changing strategies.
Verification aspect: State transition invariants monitored and logged with monotonic counters.

## CodingAgent Parallel Subagents (https://codingagent.in/parallel-subagents)
Category: Core & Agents
Isolated subagent execution runtimes tackling modular work units concurrently under strict parent orchestrator supervision.
Rationale: Accelerates massive codebase audits, documentation generation, and multi-package refactorings without cross-contaminating workspace state.
Verification aspect: Branch-isolated git worktrees merged only after merge conflict analysis and full test suite passes.

## CodingAgent Human Approval Gates (https://codingagent.in/human-approval-gates)
Category: Core & Agents
Explicit interactive checkpoints interrupting autonomous execution when an agent touches sensitive network, deployment, or database resources.
Rationale: Maintains human sovereignty over consequential actions: models propose changes, humans authorize external side effects.
Verification aspect: Cryptographic signature of operator authorization recorded in the mission ledger.

## CodingAgent Agent Observability (https://codingagent.in/agent-observability)
Category: Core & Agents
Deep structured telemetry capturing tokens, latency, tool call payloads, diffs, sandbox metrics, and verifier exit codes.
Rationale: Provides engineering teams complete transparency into agent deliberation, cost attribution, and failure forensics.
Verification aspect: OpenTelemetry-compliant spans emitted for every model invocation and tool dispatch.

## CodingAgent Durable Runtimes (https://codingagent.in/durable-runtimes)
Category: Core & Agents
Resilient execution runtimes capable of pausing, serializing, persisting to disk, and resuming missions across process restarts.
Rationale: Allows long-running multi-hour migrations or flaky network interruptions to resume seamlessly without lost context.
Verification aspect: Snapshot replay tests verifying that restored states reproduce deterministic downstream operations.

## CodingAgent Production Operations (https://codingagent.in/production-operations)
Category: Core & Agents
Operational playbooks, rate limiters, cost governors, health monitors, and emergency killswitches for running agents at scale.
Rationale: Protects cloud infrastructure budgets, prevents runaway API billings, and enforces compliance with organizational safety guidelines.
Verification aspect: Real-time circuit breakers tripping on anomalous tool invocation frequency or token consumption spikes.

## CodingAgent Model Context Protocol (https://codingagent.in/model-context-protocol)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Standardized open protocol connecting AI assistants to external data sources, developer tools, and operational environments.
Rationale: Decouples model vendors from tool implementations, enabling a universal plugin ecosystem with typed schemas.
Verification aspect: JSON-RPC schema validation on every input payload and returned result.

## CodingAgent MCP Client Architecture (https://codingagent.in/mcp-client-architecture)
Category: MCP & Integrations
The agent-side client implementation that discovers, negotiates, scopes, and governs tools exposed by external MCP servers.
Rationale: Ensures the agent consumes third-party tools through strict policy filters rather than granting blanket access.
Verification aspect: Runtime policy intersection checks prior to each tool execution.

## CodingAgent MCP Server Architecture (https://codingagent.in/mcp-server-architecture)
Category: MCP & Integrations
The server-side implementation enabling CodingAgent to export reviewed internal capabilities, compilers, and analyzers to other agents.
Rationale: Allows specialized CodingAgent subroutines to be discovered and invoked safely across diverse IDE and CLI clients.
Verification aspect: Strict JSON Schema input validation and sanitization against code injection.

## CodingAgent Bidirectional MCP (https://codingagent.in/bidirectional-mcp)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Architecture allowing agents to simultaneously act as MCP consumers and providers, forming collaborative agentic networks.
Rationale: Facilitates mesh architectures where a planning agent delegates code synthesis to a specialized local agent via MCP.
Verification aspect: Mutual TLS and capability authorization tokens between communicating agent nodes.

## CodingAgent MCP Tool Discovery (https://codingagent.in/mcp-tool-discovery)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Dynamic negotiation and registration of available tools, prompts, and resources from attached MCP server processes.
Rationale: Keeps agent context windows clean by registering tool definitions on-demand rather than dumping huge static schemas.
Verification aspect: Namespace isolation preventing malicious MCP servers from overriding built-in core safety tools.

## CodingAgent MCP Permissions (https://codingagent.in/mcp-permissions)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Granular role-based and path-based permission policies applied to individual MCP tool invocations.
Rationale: Enforces principle of least privilege, preventing read-only file servers from performing unauthorized shell side-effects.
Verification aspect: Policy evaluation matrix validating workspace boundaries and allowed HTTP domains.

## CodingAgent MCP Authentication (https://codingagent.in/mcp-authentication)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Cryptographic authentication, bearer token rotation, and secret redaction for MCP server connections.
Rationale: Prevents credential leakage into LLM prompt contexts and ensures authorized access to internal enterprise microservices.
Verification aspect: Automatic regex-based masking of secrets in tool response streams before context ingestion.

## CodingAgent MCP Transport (https://codingagent.in/mcp-transport)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Low-latency stdio, Server-Sent Events (SSE), and WebSocket transport layers supporting both local and remote MCP servers.
Rationale: Allows lightning-fast local subprocess communication alongside secure encrypted remote cloud tool hosting.
Verification aspect: Heartbeat monitoring and backpressure buffering during high-volume tool data transfers.

## CodingAgent MCP Security (https://codingagent.in/mcp-security)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Defense-in-depth security model protecting agent runtimes from malicious MCP servers, tainted outputs, and prompt poisoning.
Rationale: Recognizes external tool outputs as untrusted user input, sanitizing return strings before model ingestion.
Verification aspect: AST-based taint tracking on variables constructed from tool outputs.

## CodingAgent Building MCP Integrations (https://codingagent.in/building-mcp-integrations)
Category: MCP & Integrations
Developer guide, SDKs, and templates for wrapping custom compilers, profilers, and enterprise ticketing systems into governed MCP tools.
Rationale: Empowers engineering teams to bridge proprietary internal infrastructure into agentic workflows in minutes.
Verification aspect: Automated contract test suites verifying schema adherence for new MCP server implementations.

## CodingAgent Local LLM Coding (https://codingagent.in/local-llm-coding)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
First-class support for running state-of-the-art open coding models (DeepSeek-Coder, Qwen-Coder, Llama-Code) on local workstations.
Rationale: Keeps proprietary enterprise intellectual property 100% on developer hardware without transmitting code to third parties.
Verification aspect: Model benchmark harness measuring pass@1 accuracy on repository-specific unit tests.

## CodingAgent Ollama Integration (https://codingagent.in/ollama-integration)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Seamless integration with Ollama for zero-config local model pulls, GPU acceleration, and streaming inference.
Rationale: Provides instant developer onboarding with one-click setup across macOS Metal, Linux CUDA, and Windows ROCm.
Verification aspect: Health check probe verifying VRAM allocation and context length availability before mission dispatch.

## CodingAgent vLLM Serving (https://codingagent.in/vllm-serving)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
High-throughput self-hosted inference serving powered by PagedAttention and continuous batching for team clusters.
Rationale: Enables engineering organizations to serve hundreds of concurrent developer agent sessions on shared private GPU infrastructure.
Verification aspect: Throughput and latency SLO monitoring with automatic request queuing.

## CodingAgent llama.cpp Runtimes (https://codingagent.in/llama-cpp-runtimes)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Bare-metal C/C++ GGUF model execution with minimal memory footprint and CPU fallback optimization.
Rationale: Allows lightweight agents to run on resource-constrained edge machines, developer laptops, and CI runner nodes without discrete GPUs.
Verification aspect: Memory profile assertions preventing out-of-memory kernel panics.

## CodingAgent LM Studio (https://codingagent.in/lm-studio)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Connector for LM Studio desktop local servers, providing visual model management and OpenAI-compatible API endpoints.
Rationale: Catches developers who prefer graphical interfaces for model discovery, parameter tuning, and hardware diagnostics.
Verification aspect: Endpoint compatibility check validating tool-call formatting support.

## CodingAgent GGUF Workflows (https://codingagent.in/gguf-workflows)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Optimized pipeline for selecting, caching, and running quantized GGUF model weights tuned specifically for syntax and code generation.
Rationale: Maximizes context window size within available workstation VRAM constraints.
Verification aspect: Perplexity and syntax error rate validation across quantization tiers (Q4_K_M vs Q8_0).

## CodingAgent Quantized Models (https://codingagent.in/quantized-models)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Evaluation benchmarks and best practices for running 4-bit, 5-bit, and 8-bit quantized models without degrading refactoring fidelity.
Rationale: Guides developers toward optimal precision trade-offs for code editing versus architectural planning tasks.
Verification aspect: Automated syntax parsing on generated diffs to ensure no token truncation or invalid grammar.

## CodingAgent VRAM-Aware Routing (https://codingagent.in/vram-aware-routing)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Intelligent router that dynamically inspects host GPU memory, context size requirements, and task complexity before choosing a model.
Rationale: Routes lightweight syntax fixes to fast 7B local models while escalating massive cross-file refactors to larger local or cloud models.
Verification aspect: Real-time NVML/Metal VRAM telemetry checks before dispatching token batches.

## CodingAgent Offline Embeddings (https://codingagent.in/offline-embeddings)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Local vector embedding models and lightweight embedded vector stores for indexing private codebases offline.
Rationale: Enables semantic search, code symbol lookup, and reference graph resolution without sending index chunks to external vector APIs.
Verification aspect: Cosine similarity recall validation against verified symbol ground-truth pairs.

## CodingAgent Air-Gapped Agents (https://codingagent.in/air-gapped-agents)
Category: Local LLMs & Routing
Hardened agent distribution packaged for defense, banking, and critical infrastructure environments with zero internet access.
Rationale: Guarantees that no external telemetry, DNS lookups, or package dependencies can compromise high-security air-gapped enclaves.
Verification aspect: Network namespace lockdown with zero-byte egress verification in sandbox tests.

## CodingAgent AI Agent Security (https://codingagent.in/ai-agent-security)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Comprehensive threat modeling and defense architecture addressing the unique attack vectors introduced by autonomous coding agents.
Rationale: Protects the developer machine and enterprise pipelines from weaponized repository files and compromised packages.
Verification aspect: Continuous penetration testing against agent tool surfaces and sandbox escapes.

## CodingAgent Prompt Injection Defenses (https://codingagent.in/prompt-injection-defenses)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Multi-layer defense isolating untrusted repository strings, issues, and PR comments from executive system instructions.
Rationale: Prevents indirect prompt injections embedded in READMEs or dependencies from hijacking agent execution authority.
Verification aspect: Strict separation of control and data planes using structured XML/JSON envelope formats.

## CodingAgent Secure Tool Calling (https://codingagent.in/secure-tool-calling)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Strict schema enforcement, argument validation, and parameter sanitization applied prior to executing any tool call.
Rationale: Prevents shell injection and path traversal vulnerabilities from being triggered by generative model outputs.
Verification aspect: Path normalization and canonicalization verifying targets remain within the designated task workspace.

## CodingAgent Agent Sandboxing (https://codingagent.in/agent-sandboxing)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Lightweight containerized (Docker, bubblewrap, gVisor) sandboxes enclosing code execution, compilation, and test runs.
Rationale: Isolates malicious or buggy code changes from altering the developer host filesystem or accessing user home directories.
Verification aspect: Filesystem and process tree isolation monitored with seccomp filter profiles.

## CodingAgent Network Egress Controls (https://codingagent.in/network-egress-controls)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Default-deny network firewall allowing agent tool requests only to approved, domain-allowlisted endpoints.
Rationale: Stops data exfiltration attacks where compromised code attempts to curl environment variables to remote adversary servers.
Verification aspect: Packet inspection logging and DNS filtering on all container egress interfaces.

## CodingAgent Secrets Isolation (https://codingagent.in/secrets-isolation)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Fine-grained secret broker that injects credentials only at the instant of authorized tool calls and immediately scrubs them.
Rationale: Ensures API tokens, private SSH keys, and cloud credentials never enter model prompt histories or telemetry spans.
Verification aspect: Memory wiping and automated entropy scans on prompt and context buffers.

## CodingAgent Repository Permissions (https://codingagent.in/repository-permissions)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Granular file and branch access policies restricting which folders an agent can read, modify, or delete.
Rationale: Prevents unintentional changes to mission-critical infrastructure-as-code files, root manifests, or branch protections.
Verification aspect: Pre-commit git hooks validating diffs against declared task scope manifests.

## CodingAgent Approval Policy Design (https://codingagent.in/approval-policy-design)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Declarative policy rules categorizing actions into automatic ALLOW, interactive ASK, and absolute DENY tiers.
Rationale: Balances developer velocity with ironclad safety by automating low-risk operations while gating high-impact changes.
Verification aspect: Static policy evaluator compiling YAML rules into deterministic runtime decision trees.

## CodingAgent Audit Logs & Provenance (https://codingagent.in/audit-logs-provenance)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Immutable, tamper-evident cryptographic logs recording every model prompt, tool call argument, output diff, and verification hash.
Rationale: Provides compliance and security teams complete forensic evidence of software authorship and supply-chain integrity.
Verification aspect: Merkle tree hashing and signed SLSA provenance attestations for generated release artifacts.

## CodingAgent Secure MCP Servers (https://codingagent.in/secure-mcp-servers)
Category: Security & Sovereignty
Hardening standards and security audits for authoring, running, and publishing Model Context Protocol server tools.
Rationale: Prevents tool injection vulnerabilities from turning external MCP integrations into remote code execution vectors.
Verification aspect: Automated vulnerability scanning of MCP server dependencies and JSON-RPC endpoints.

## CodingAgent Independent Verification (https://codingagent.in/independent-verification)
Category: Verification & Memory
The golden principle that model self-evaluations cannot be trusted: code changes must pass independent compilers and tests.
Rationale: Eliminates false positives where models hallucinate that code builds without ever invoking the compiler.
Verification aspect: Exit-code verification from non-LLM native tools (tsc, cargo check, pytest, go test).

## CodingAgent Build Verification (https://codingagent.in/build-verification)
Category: Verification & Memory
Automated build pipeline invocation inside clean task sandboxes to verify package resolution and compilation success.
Rationale: Guarantees that syntax and dependency modifications produce deployable binaries before a task is marked complete.
Verification aspect: Hermetic build artifact generation with zero compilation warnings.

## CodingAgent Typecheck Verification (https://codingagent.in/typecheck-verification)
Category: Verification & Memory
Rigorous static type analysis ensuring strict adherence to interfaces, non-nullability, and function signature contracts.
Rationale: Catches subtle runtime bugs and interface mismatch errors instantly across large polyglot codebases.
Verification aspect: Full repository typecheck pass (e.g. tsc --noEmit, mypy, dialyzer).

## CodingAgent Unit Test Verification (https://codingagent.in/unit-test-verification)
Category: Verification & Memory
Execution of existing test suites and generation of new unit tests to confirm behavioral fixes without regressions.
Rationale: Enforces software engineering best practices by proving that bug fixes fix the bug without breaking adjacent logic.
Verification aspect: Differential code coverage reports and green test runners.

## CodingAgent Browser Verification (https://codingagent.in/browser-verification)
Category: Verification & Memory
Headless browser execution (Playwright, Puppeteer) capturing screenshots, DOM snapshots, and console logs of frontend UI changes.
Rationale: Verifies visual rendering, responsive layout fidelity, and browser runtime console errors.
Verification aspect: Pixel-diff regression analysis and assertion of zero unhandled window error events.

## CodingAgent Artifact Hashing (https://codingagent.in/artifact-hashing)
Category: Verification & Memory
Cryptographic SHA-256 fingerprinting of all inputs, intermediate diffs, tool outputs, and produced binary artifacts.
Rationale: Enables deterministic caching, instant replay of identical tasks, and verification of supply chain integrity.
Verification aspect: Content-addressable storage index matching expected cryptographic digests.

## CodingAgent Agent Memory Architecture (https://codingagent.in/agent-memory-architecture)
Category: Verification & Memory
Hierarchical memory system separating short-term scratchpad context, working task memory, and long-term repository knowledge.
Rationale: Prevents context window overflow while preserving critical architectural lessons learned in prior debugging sessions.
Verification aspect: Memory retrieval relevance evaluations and garbage collection of stale ephemeral records.

## CodingAgent Working & Mission Memory (https://codingagent.in/working-mission-memory)
Category: Verification & Memory
Structured state stores tracking active task objectives, hypotheses tested, failed approaches, and remaining TODOs.
Rationale: Prevents the agent from repeating previously failed edits and maintains momentum across multi-turn interactions.
Verification aspect: Monotonic convergence metrics toward accepted criteria.

## CodingAgent Agent Skills & Versioning (https://codingagent.in/agent-skills-versioning)
Category: Verification & Memory
System for extracting, reviewing, versioning, and sharing successful multi-step agent workflows as reusable SKILL.md modules.
Rationale: Transforms one-off debugging successes into institutional engineering capability accessible to the entire team.
Verification aspect: Semantic versioning and automated regression testing of skill scripts on test repositories.

## CodingAgent Context Compaction (https://codingagent.in/context-compaction)
Category: Verification & Memory
Intelligent AST-aware token pruning, diff summarization, and context compaction algorithms for ultra-long conversations.
Rationale: Reduces model token costs by up to 80% while preserving essential symbol definitions and recent test failure traces.
Verification aspect: Information retention benchmarks testing agent ability to answer questions from compacted history.
